title: Keep a levelled source's first-person voice
statement: When levelling a primary source for younger readers, keep its first-person voice, the property that justifies using it, so the firsthand and secondhand contrast survives.
detail: A grade-4 reading plan uses period letters and logs as primary sources, and its plan evaluation found that their authentic 18th-century syntax would exceed the band's 940L ceiling unless adapted. Its generation contract adapts such sources to the band while keeping the first-person source voice, because the standard being taught, contrasting firsthand and secondhand accounts, depends on that property surviving the levelling.

evidence.quote: **Where the spec calls for a primary source (U5 log, U6 letter), adapt to band while preserving the first-person source voice**, the firsthand/secondhand contrast (RI.4.6) must survive the leveling.
authentic 18th-century syntax will exceed 940L unless adapted
must preserve the firsthand-source property (RI.4.6) that justifies using them.
